common_name: Royal Velvet Amaryllis (Deep Burgundy-Red Large-Flowered Amaryllis)

planting.note: Pot bulbs for indoor holiday forcing 6-8 weeks before desired bloom, or plant outdoors in fall in zone 8-11 gardens.

directions: Pot the bulb with the top third exposed in a snug container and keep barely moist until the flower stalk emerges, then increase watering as growth accelerates. Royal Velvet produces some of the darkest, most saturated burgundy-red trumpet blooms in the amaryllis trade, with a plush, light-absorbing sheen that reads almost black in low light next to brighter reds. After flowering, let foliage grow on in bright light to recharge the bulb for next season rather than discarding it, since well-fed bulbs rebloom reliably for years. Outdoors in warm zones it can be left in the ground as a permanent border perennial.

planting.note: Pot the oversized bulb 6-8 weeks ahead of a target bloom date, giving it a correspondingly larger pot than standard amaryllis bulbs.

directions: Spartacus is grown primarily for sheer flower size, producing jumbo bright-red trumpets on a thick, sturdy scape, so it needs a wide, heavy pot to keep from tipping as blooms open. Stake the stalk if growing indoors under lower light, since the oversized flowers put real weight on the stem. Let foliage mature fully after bloom to recharge the correspondingly large bulb before its dry dormancy rest. Outdoors in zone 9-11 it makes a bold specimen clump at the back of a bulb border.
